messages:
maya: Heads-up — customer cust-824 reporting streaming responses cut off mid-event. They get a handful of tokens then the stream closes. They pasted client output: partial JSON then connection reset. Server logs show write errors (EAGAIN / EPIPE).

sam: Oof. Any correlation with traffic spikes or autoscale events?

maya: Not during peak. Happened over a steady low-throughput session. I grabbed the server logs around the timeframe: 
```
[2026-11-02T14:22:10Z] INFO stream-session id=... wrote 2048 bytes
[2026-11-02T14:22:10Z] WARN stream-session id=... write() returned EAGAIN
[2026-11-02T14:22:10Z] ERROR stream-session id=... send failed: EPIPE
[2026-11-02T14:22:11Z] INFO stream-session id=... session closed by peer (code 1006)
```

nina: Customer says their client is a thin websocket->SSE proxy in Node. They added throttling for testing and the issue repros quickly.

liam: Can you share a repro command? I want to mimic the slow consumer.

maya: Repro steps I used:
1) Start Redwood streaming endpoint with model=X (hosted).
2) Run this Node snippet to simulate a slow reader (delays reading body chunks):
```js
const http = require('http');
http.get('https://api.redwood.example/stream?model=X', res => {
  res.on('data', chunk => {
    console.log('got chunk', chunk.toString('utf8').slice(0,50));
    // artificially slow consumer
    const ms = 2500; // 2.5s pauses per chunk
    Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms);
  });
  res.on('end', () => console.log('end'));
});
```
This reliably triggers EAGAIN in ~5-10s for me.

sam: Nice repro. So it's the consumer reads too slowly and socket send buffers fill up. Do we have limits on how long we hold the connection open when we can't make progress?

ingest-bot: Observability note: stream-latency-alerts fired 3x in the last 24h for cust-824; avg send stalls 1.9s, 95p 4.3s.

nina: On the client side, Chrome showed the TLS connection remained open but bytes stopped arriving. The proxy wasn't closing the connection; it was just not reading which caused the upstream to stall.

liam: From runtime POV, when `send()` returns EAGAIN we should retry after epoll signals writable. But if the client never reads, the kernel buffer saturates and repeated attempts eventually hit EPIPE when peer resets or we call close while unsent data exists. We should be failing the session more gracefully (controlled abort after X backlog ms) and emit a clear metric.

support_lead: Customer also reported a billing spike because their retry logic re-requested generation after perceived failures. We need to both fix infra and coordinate credits.

maya: Repro of the billing spike: they had a 5s client timeout and retried generation requests while the first stream was still attempting to drain. That led to duplicate token consumption on our side.

sam: Action items I propose:
- short term: implement server-side hard-timeout for stalled write (e.g., 20s of consecutive EAGAIN) and return an explicit 503 with retry-advice header so clients don't double-retry.
- medium: emit metric stream_write_backpressure_{count,ms} and an alert when a session exceeds threshold.
- long term: push a change to SDKs to use idempotency keys for streaming start so retries don't double-bill.

liam: Agreed. Also we can try reducing chunk sizes/flush frequency from runtime to avoid large bursts filling kernel buffers. Another knob: tune SO_SNDBUF per socket or TCP_QUICKACK to improve drain, but that's platform-level and risky.

maya: I tested a patch that forces smaller flushes and introduced a 50ms backoff after the first EAGAIN; it reduced occurrences in my local runs. Patch: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/1839 (link internal).

nina: For the customer: recommend they implement exponential backoff for client retries and support Last-Event-ID semantics so reconnects can resume where left off. Also ask them to increase their client read buffer / ensure their proxy forwards data promptly.

support_lead: I'll open a billing ticket for cust-824. We should offer a one-time credit and explain steps we're taking. @maya can you draft the customer-facing note?

maya: Drafting now. Will include repro steps, suggested client changes, and timeline for infra mitigations.

opsbot: NOTE: Temporary mitigation deployed to runtime: 20s stall detect + explicit 503 + "X-Redwood-Retry-After" header. Rollout: canary 5% -> 100% in 15m.

sam: Thanks. Once canary is green, let's monitor stream_write_backpressure metrics and billing anomalies for cust-824.

liam: Also let's add an automated integration test that simulates a slow consumer (2.5s chunk delay) and asserts we don't hang forever and we return a clear error path.

maya: Adding test and customer note to the ticket. Will ping again after billing update and canary completes. :thumbsup:

support_lead: Thx team. Escalation owner: @maya.
